old_title: Live: Dockers rattled with red-hot Swans on top in blockbuster prelim
new_title: 'Devastated' Swans' tumultuous season ended by stirring Freo fightback
old_text:
Thu, 3 Sept, 8:10 pm, Final score, Dockers 40, Hawks 72
live
AFL live updates: Sydney vs Fremantle preliminary final - blog, scores and stats
Sydney is continuing its fairytale AFL finals campaign, with the unfancied Swans out-muscling minor premier Fremantle in a frenetic preliminary final at the SCG. Follow live.
Follow the live blog below, keep up to date with all the latest stats in our ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio coverage.
Submit a comment or question
Live updates
Sydney vs Fremantle - live scoreboard
New: Filters
Choose what information you see below by using filters
'Youthful exuberance': Grundy on Jackson's taunting
The ruck battle has been absolutely fascinating out there between Brodie Grundy and Luke Jackson.
After winning a free kick in a marking contest in the first quarter, Jackson clapped in the veteran Swans big man's face.
Grundy has responded with a strong half of football. He's got five touches, 10 hitouts and two clearances, while Jackson has six touches, 14 hitouts and one clearance.
Grundy is asked by Fox Footy's Brad Johnson about Jackson's clap and says: "Youthful exuberance, love it".
Key Event
HT: Sydney 7.6 (48) leads Fremantle 4.5 (29)
Absolutely no love lost between these two sides as they walk off the ground at half-time.
Pat Voss has his first possession of the match after receiving a free kick seconds before the siren, and amid boos, his set shot from outside 50 fails to register a score.
Voss receiving plenty of lip there and Tom Papley gets into the Dockers as he goes into the Swans huddle.
An excellent first half from the Swans as they take a 19-point lead into the main break.
The Dockers lead the inside 50 count 31-27 and the clearance count 22-13, but their ball movement going forward has been shoddy to say the least.
Errol Gulden is the leading ball-winner on the ground with 17 touches, while Caleb Serong leads the way for Freo with 13 touches and five clearances.
Gulden has also laid four tackles, with the Swans leading the tackle count 33-30. They've laid 12 tackles inside 50, which is the most they've ever had in the opening half of a final.
Dockers continue to blow it going inside 50
Freo continues to blast away as they try and go inside 50 and the Swans defence is eating it up right now.
They've had enough of the footy around the ground, but the attacking entries are leaving a lot to be desired.
Two minutes to go in the half, can they find a goal from somewhere?
McInerney drills set shot after free kick
Justin McInerney causes the SCG to explode once again as he drills a set shot from 40m out on a tricky angle.
Sydney with just a little bit more intensity at the footy right now, and they're getting rewarded.
A loose ball inside 50 for the Swans and Andy Brayshaw gives away the free kick after holding McInerney without the footy.
Freo's big men are floundering out there so far.
Pat Voss yet to have a possession, while Josh Treacy and Jye Amiss have combined for just six.
Dudley with the quick response for Freo!
My goodness did the Dockers need that goal!
They get the centre bounce clearance after the Cleary goal and Hayden Young stands up in a tackle and dishes off to Isaiah Dudley, who drills it on the run.
Two goals apiece in this quarter so far.
Cleary drills the set shot to perfection!
Barry Hall's kids are in the stands with their tops off again as Caiden Cleary sails home a set shot!
More terrific forward pressure again as Shai Bolton's snap out of the forward pocket lands in Cleary's lap.
"I'm not sure I've seen their senior core as rattled as this. Sydney have rattled them," David King says on Freo's performance on Fox Footy.
Frederick ends Freo's goal drought after free kick
A chorus of boos ring around the SCG as Michael Frederick snaps home Freo's third goal of the match.
Angus Sheldrick was pinged for what the umpire deemed to be a high fend-off as Frederick attempted to tackle him.
That's a much-needed goal for Frederick and Freo to just stay in touch.
McDonald extends Sydney's game-high lead
The Swans go from end-to-end again and get another goal!
Great stuff by Billy Cootee on the wing as he fights hard to keep a ball alive and gets it forward towards Tom Papley.
Papley snaps towards Logan McDonald in the square and Oscar McDonald gives away the free kick for front-on contact.
McDonald snaps truly from close range to give the Swans a 23-point lead. They've kicked five straight!
Three missed set shots for Freo to start second term
We've had three set shots from Freo that haven't gone through so far.
Two of them to Jye Amiss and the other to Michael Frederick.
Rowbottom with an early miss after another forward 50 tackle
James Rowbottom with a narrow miss to the right after winning a free kick inside 50 following a lovely tackle on Alex Pearce.
The Swans really could've been much further ahead had they kicked a little straighter.
Nevertheless, this 17-point lead is a game-high.
Murphy or Midphy Reid?
Hi Chris. Just wondering, if Murphy Reid is terrified of physical contact, allergic to defensive effort AND unable to hit a target by foot, what exactly is he providing to this team? If Freo get up here they should think about replacing him with O'Meara or even Brennan Cox for the GF.
- Anonymous
Freo's All-Australian was another one who was pretty quiet in the opening term.
He's had six touches but has had little to no impact on the game.
Will the Swans regret their inaccuracy?
Good start from the Swannies, but they could have kicked well clear. Freo will come back, Sydney might regret it later!
- Allan
It's a valid point Allan, particularly with those two posters coming on very, very gettable shots.
They'd have backed Papley to kick his missed set shot as well.
It really could've been a lot uglier for Freo at this stage.
Key Event
QT: Sydney 4.5 (29) leads Fremantle 2.1 (13)
Another brilliant quarter at the SCG by the Swans sees them take a 16-point lead into the first change.
Freo had what would've been just about the perfect start by kicking the first two goals early, but Sydney's response has been absolutely immense.
The Swans' pressure has been absolutely manic, and they've swallowed up the Dockers all around the ground.
Sydney has laid 16 tackles to 11 including eight of those coming in their forward 50.
The Swans have a slight edge in the inside 50 count (17-16), while the Dockers lead the clearance count (8-6).
Sydney's Errol Gulden is the leading ball-winner on the ground with eight disposals, while Caleb Serong has added five touches and a game-high three clearances.
Logan McDonald has also been lively up forward for the Swans and leads all players with four score involvements.
Freo's big forward trio virtually non-existent so far, they'll need to lift to get out of this hole.
Dattoli with another poster as Swans continue heat
Sydney's pressure factor right now is at 319, I don't know that I've ever seen that figure that high.
Freo lucky not to be further behind as Jesse Dattoli hits the post after winning a free kick inside 50.
The Swans are absolutely ripping the Dockers up on transition last nith.
Nine scoring shots to three says it all.
Hanily dribbles home Sydney's fourth in a row!
Tom Hanily with some brilliant crumbing at the foot of the big key forwards!
A lovely kick off halfback from Jai Serong finds Logan McDonald on the wing and McDonald rolls around and sends it forwards.
Tom Papley and Charlie Curnow win a crucial two-on-two at half-forward and Papley sends it forward before Hanily's crumbing goal.
Sydney's forward 50 pressure is manic right now
The Swans have six tackles inside their forward 50 to Freo's two.
They've had nine inside 50 entries in the last 10 minutes, and lead the overall count 13-12.
McLean hits the post as Swans' positive momentum continues
Hayden McLean with a poor miss as he hits the right-hand upright from virtually directly in front.
Sydney's forward 50 entries have been excellent so far. They've got two marks inside 50 to Freo's one.
McDonald makes it three straight for the Swans
Logan McDonald sneaks home a set shot from 35m out from a slight angle and the SCG erupts again!
Excellent stuff from Braeden Campbell as he kept a ball on the wing alive with a deft tap and then Charlie Curnow finds McDonald with a lovely kick inside 50.
That's the beauty of Curnow, he's equally adept at setting goals up as he is kicking them himself.
Free kick denies Dudley an early goal
We've got our first big call of the evening!
Isaiah Dudley snaps at goal and the ball sails through as Joel Hamling gets bundled over inside the square by Jye Amiss.
However, the umpire blows the whistle and gives Hamling the free kick.
I've got to say I think that one was there.

Thu, 3 Sept, 8:10 pm, Final score, Dockers 40, Hawks 72
Fremantle through to first AFL grand final since 2013 after stunning final-quarter comeback
Fremantle has pulled off a sensational last-quarter comeback to surge into the AFL grand final with a tense 12-point win over Sydney.
Trailing by 27 points late in the third quarter, the Dockers kicked the last six goals of their preliminary final to win 12.11 (83) to 10.11 (71) at the SCG.
Fremantle advances to the second grand final in club history, where they will meet either Hawthorn or Brisbane.
Justin Longmuir's men were staring down the barrel of an early exit before Hayden Young converted a difficult set shot after the three-quarter time siren, and were full of running in a gripping finish.
Young (28 disposals), Andrew Brayshaw (29), Caleb Serong (28) and Shai Bolton (two goals) were instrumental in the victory.
But it wasn't assured until the dying stages, when Isaiah Dudley ran into an open goal with less than two minutes on the clock.
"Words can't describe how proud I am of everyone for stepping up," Fremantle captain Alex Pearce told Channel 7.
"There were just so many moments where guys stood up under the fiercest of pressure.
"We played our best footy in the last quarter when everything was against us."
Luke Jackson finished with two goals in an entertaining ruck battle with Brodie Grundy.
Dudley's second major was the Dockers' fifth of a dominant final quarter, in which Patrick Voss's huge fend-off and checkside goal on the run was a highlight.
"[Our forwards] were beaten early, and it was hurting us a little bit," Pearce said.
"Our ball use into the forward line was diabolical at times. We were just kicking it to the red jumper.
"But wow, our forwards stood up [in the final quarter]. They stood up like big men."
Sydney's brave effort came without injured captain Callum Mills and the five stars banned in the fallout from the Pullman Hotel scandal.
Errol Gulden (36 disposals) was brilliant in setting up their lead, with Logan McDonald (three goals) dangerous in attack.
"It's gut-wrenching, devastating, but I'm overwhelmed with pride in what we've been able to do over the last couple weeks," Swans stand-in captain Dane Rampe said.
"We didn't get that result tonight, but I felt over the last couple of weeks we took a couple of steps in the right direction towards [getting] back respect and trust of not only our fans and our club, but the AFL community in general."
Swans coach appeared emotional during his post-match press conference, but spoke of his pride in the group.
"I'm extremely proud. To put on a performance like that, I'm just extremely proud of everyone uniting and galvanising to get our season to the last game, and we fell short," Cox said.
"It is raw, but that is footy, footy is a hard game. I learnt a hell of a lot. I've got a chance to really reflect on the season we've had.
"We want to be playing these games of footy every year, that's what we strive for. I love prelim finals.
"We've got to learn, and I do as well, and we'll spend the off-season doing that. They've been really supportive and wanted to action everything we wanted to put in place. They've just been really hungry to improve.
"It's hard to say it's a missed opportunity when you play a really good footy team."
AAP

That's where we'll leave things for tonight!
Thank you for spending your evening with us for what was a thrilling win for Freo!
Join us again tomorrow as Hawthorn and Brisbane battle for the right to face the Dockers.
I'll be on hand again to bring you all the live action as it happens.
See you then!
Dean Cox looks emotional at the post-game press conference
A lot in this post-game chat from Dean Cox, who looks as though he might have shed some tears in the locker room with his team before getting to the podium.
"I'm extremely proud. To put on a performance like that, I'm just extremely proud of everyone uniting and galvanising to get our season to the last game, and we fell short.
"To Freo's credit, they ramped up towards the end of the third. We were in a really good position for three and a bit quarters, but this time of the year, you can't give a team any sort of momentum.
"They outnumbered and we blasted out of our back half and they got repeat entries and took their moments, that's what good teams too.
"I thought our pressure on the ball carrier and the system that we played stood up.
"I've been really proud of the ability to play the players we have all throughout the year. When they weren't playing throughout the year, they acquitted of themselves really well.
"It is raw, but that is footy, footy is a hard game. I learnt a hell of a lot. I've got a chance to really reflect on the season we've had.
"We want to be playing these games of footy every year, that's what we strive for. I love prelim finals.
"We've got to learn, and I do as well, and we'll spend the off-season doing that. They've been really supportive and wanted to action everything we wanted to put in place. They've just been really hungry to improve.
"It's hard to say it's a missed opportunity when you play a really good footy team.
"Prelims are big games and there is a lot at stake because there is a grand final next week.
"The older players, they certainly understand that they don't just come around every year. They're hard to get to, so that'll settle in the next few days."
Cox is asked about what lies ahead for Dane Rampe, who was very emotional after the match.
"I can't speak highly enough of what Dane has done for our football club ever since he's been here.
"He's a club favourite, a fan favourite. His emotional intelligence is as high as I've seen.
"He leads really strongly and it's just unfortunate that we couldn't get done for him.
"He's earned the right to say if he wants to play on or if he doesn't, and we'll have the conversations from there."
A look back at the manic final few minutes
If you missed the ending to this match, here's how it panned out:
Good luck trying to fly from Perth to Melbourne
Stuie is not happy with the umpiring in the final term
Not a single free kick to the Swans in the final quarter.
- StuieD
What a con. Disgraceful by the Umpires. They have umpired Sydney out of the game, whether through incompetence or, as I suspect, deliberately.
- StuieD
A disgrace. An absolute disgrace. Sydney absolutely ripped off.
- StuieD
What was the free kick count in the last quarter?
- StuieD
Jackson says Freo GF appearance 'dream come true'
What a moment for Luke Jackson, who grew up a Fremantle fan, and now gets to represent his Dockers in a grand final!
Jackson was a very young buck when he reached the big dance with Melbourne in 2021, but will be one of the main men next Saturday.
Bolton opens up on Brayshaw's letter to teammates
Longmuir speaks after riding the rollercoaster
Fremantle coach Justin Longmuir says he "rode the rollercoaster" tonight.
"We were able to hit the scoreboard and put the pressure on them," he tells Fox Footy.
"It [Young's goal on 3QT] just gave us a little bit of a boost, and we probably needed that.
"We jumped into the last quarter the way we wanted to and got field position.
"I wouldn't have wanted [the ball] in anyone else's hands, put it that way.
The Pullman Five end up costing the Swans
What could have been for Sydney... those five outs would have been good to have.
- Jeremy
Definitely would've made a difference tonight Jeremy. I can imagine Nick Blakey's run off halfback in particular when Freo started dominating territory.
What a shame after such a good season for the Swans. The remaining players fought so hard, but they didn't have enough firepower tonight.
It was like rocking up to a gunfight with a butter knife in the end.
The Dockers represented in the theatre!
Am sitting in His Majesty's Theatre in Perth watching a ballet...during interval an audience member got up and squealed, waving her freo scarf...and that's how the whole audience knew!!
- Avi
A look at some of the big individual performances
Here are your top three players on the ground according to the AFL's ranking points:
- Errol Gulden (SYD): 36 disposals, eight tackles, seven inside 50s, five clearances, 766m gained
- Hayden Young (FRE): 28 disposals, seven tackles, seven score involvements, five inside 50s, four clearances
- Shai Bolton (FRE): 20 disposals, eight tackles, seven score involvements, seven inside 50s, three clearances, 2.0
Alex Pearce reacts to Fremantle's comeback win
Is this Rampe's final game for Sydney?
Dane Rampe looks the most emotional of all the Swans after that one.
He's very teary and has a wave to the fans in the stands before walking off the ground.
The 36-year-old is out of contract, I wonder if he's played his last game for the Swans.
The final numbers from Fremantle's prelim win
Here's a look at the final team numbers, and in the end these numbers show that Freo's dominance eventually told on the scoreboard:
- Disposals: Fremantle 369-314
- Inside 50s: Fremantle 67-49
- Clearances: Fremantle 44-30
- Centre Clearances: Fremantle 12-6
- Contested Possessions: Fremantle 162-133
- Marks: Fremantle 71-44
- Marks Inside 50: Fremantle 9-6
- Contested Marks: Fremantle 17-8
- Tackles: Sydney 80-64
- Tackles in Forward 50: Sydney 19-17
- One Percenters: Sydney 57-41
Incredible scenes on the ground after that one!
The Dockers are understandably absolutely chuffed after that one.
Hayden Young speaks to Fox Footy, he was the firestarter after kicking that goal on the boundary on the three-quarter time siren, and calls the kick a "fluke".
I'm not too sure about that.
There is a massive Freo contingent in the stands and the players are going around exchanging high fives with those sitting boundaryside.
Justin Longmuir looks absolutely proud as punch out there and rightly so.
Key Event
FT: Fremantle 12.11 (83) defeats Sydney 10.11 (71)
The Dockers have done it! They are through to their first grand final since 2013 after an absolute SCG heist!
Luke Jackson jumps into the arms of Shai Bolton and that ecstasy is mirrored by absolute devastation from the Swans.
Dane Rampe on his haunches and in tears as he shares a hug with Tom McCartin.
Shai Bolton has blood streaming from above his left eye as he chats to Eddie Betts, describing this win as "special".
He was outstanding in the final quarter with two goals to get this comeback underway.
It was a complete final quarter avalanche from the league's best team all year.
They kicked 5.4 to 0.1 in the final quarter to steal this.
Papley hits the post!
Oh my goodness, Papley almost kicks an incredible goal from congestion, but the ball bounces and hits the post.
The Swans need two goals in a minute. I don't think it's going to happen.
Dudley wins a huge free kick, then seals the deal!
Isaiah Dudley wins a free kick for high contact in the middle of the ground.
He then works his way forward and receives the handpass from Murphy Reid and drills the goal to put the Dockers into the grand final!
The Dockers have kicked 5.3 to 0.0 for the quarter. What a comeback it's been!
Freo by 12 points with 1:46 remaining on the clock.
Three minutes to go
It's a ball up inside 50 for Fremantle. One score will probably do it for the Dockers.
The Swans scoreless in the final quarter so far.

Key Event QT: Sydney 4.5 (29) leads Fremantle 2.1 (13) Another brilliant quarter at the SCG by the Swans sees them take a 16-point lead into the first change. Freo had what would've been just about the perfect start by kicking the first two goals early, but Sydney's response has been absolutely immense. The Swans' pressure has been absolutely manic, and they've swallowed up the Dockers all around the ground. Sydney has laid 16 tackles to 11 including eight of those coming in their forward 50. The Swans have a slight edge in the inside 50 count (17-16), while the Dockers lead the clearance count (8-6). Sydney's Errol Gulden is the leading ball-winner on the ground with eight disposals, while Caleb Serong has added five touches and a game-high three clearances. Logan McDonald has also been lively up forward for the Swans and leads all players with four score involvements. Freo's big forward trio virtually non-existent so far, they'll need to lift to get out of this hole.
